_comment: The frozen high-level suite: as automation grows, these expectations are
pinned so no change can silently lose the working version. tools/owi-selftest
runs every section; CI fails if any item drifts.
This file is EVOLUTIONARY by design: when a lived failure teaches a lesson,
freeze it here as a fixture and bump the version (v1 -> v2 -> ...). Never
edit an old lesson away — supersede it. Each fixture may carry a
'provenance' naming the run that taught it.
Mechanical checklist fixtures assert the verdict of tools/owi-do's own
check engine: expect true (pass), false (fail), or null (needs a judge).

check_engine_fixtures.output: The thermal node model is exposed through a wasm ABI.
Nothing about heat here at all.
See you at the review on Friday.
check_engine_fixtures.provenance: first reduced-inspection run, 2026-08-07: the checklist writer quoted its needle, the literal match kept the quotes, and a correct output was wrongly rejected (root cause: harness). Surrounding quotes are stripped from contains: needles ever since.
truncated-json shape seen in early gpt-5-mini rejections

check_engine_fixtures.item: reads as a finished changelog entry, not questions back to the author
check_engine_fixtures.provenance: first live split run, 2026-08-07: haiku asked clarifying questions instead of drafting; only a judged item caught it — free-form items MUST go to an independent judge, never silently pass

serve_gate_expectations._why: binding beyond localhost exposes an execution endpoint; the token gate is the lock. A request without the token must be turned away, and localhost mode must stay gate-free.

qc_expectations._why: lean inspection, CSP-1 style: 100% inspection while qualifying, skip-lot sampling once proven, any worker-caused failure resets. These constants and the sampling semantics are the quality-control contract.

sampling_fixtures.provenance: under reduced inspection a sampled-out judgement item must not block acceptance — that is the lean discount
mechanical items never come off the line: they still reject under reduced inspection

role_order_expectations._why: the management structure itself: specs (checklists, splits) are written from the TOP of the roster, judging is done from the BOTTOM by a non-maker. A refactor must never swap the two ladders' directions.

auto_checklist_fixtures.provenance: auto-written checklists are cleaned like planner parts: trimmed, empties dropped, capped at 4

raw.summary: Extract the profile fields as JSON

planner_fixtures.provenance: a planner naming an unknown skill must reject the whole split

_why: The stdin payload is the WHOLE task. Agentic CLIs inherit the
invoking directory and can be hijacked by whatever repo they land
in — a worker once answered 'I can't reach the docs from here'
after wandering the invoking repo.
The second lesson cost real evidence. Workers ran from the owi home
.owi-quick/, which sits INSIDE this repo, and agentic CLIs read
standing instructions from every directory above them. This repo's
CLAUDE.md tells any session it is the router, so a worker obeyed it
and replied asking whether to route the task instead of doing it.
The checklist failed, the blame landed on the model, and the ledger
learned something false about worker:sonnet-4-5/code.
Proof, same model and prompt, only the directory differing: asked
its role from .owi-quick/ it answered 'Router.', from a scratch
directory 'Worker.' Workers now execute from a fresh scratch
directory with no instruction file at or above it.
The old fixture passed throughout because it used a temporary home
with nothing above it — it never reproduced the hazard. This one
plants the instruction file above the home on purpose.

blame_expectations._why: a model never replies with literally nothing — empty runner output is plumbing (CLI collision, auth, crash-with-zero) and must be recorded as environment, never checked against the worker. Learned 2026-08-08: two rejections were misattributed to workers during concurrent CLI runs.

escalation_fixtures.provenance: first attempt goes to the cheapest runnable worker
a rejection escalates to the quality option, not the next-cheapest — the failure is evidence the job was harder than its price
an unrunnable quality option falls back to the next untried runnable worker
when everyone has been tried, iteration ends — bounded, never a loop

entries.detail: confidential leak that must never ride along

prevention_fixtures.provenance: environment/harness failures must never become prevention notes; no note to a model fixes broken plumbing; confidential entries are excluded even when their cause is the worker's

privacy_expectations._why: confidentiality is a gate, not a preference: a task above a worker's clearance must turn that worker away whatever it costs, and the local zero-price worker is the one cleared for confidential content. Prevention memory must never carry confidential task text into future prompts.

skill_coverage_expectations._why: comprehensiveness: every skill in the taxonomy must have at least one seeded worker — a skill nobody can be staffed for is a promise the index cannot keep. Grown from the role rosters people hand-build in agent workspaces (planner, architect, debugger, designer).

_why: The ask page is a static file with no server, so it carries a second
implementation of the decision rule in JavaScript. Two copies of a
money path drift silently unless something holds them together.
tools/check_page_math.py runs the block in node and asserts it
returns the engine's exact eligible set, order, and micros on a
pristine ledger; this frozen entry keeps the block extractable so
that check can never be quietly disabled by refactoring the page.
The page ranks on public evidence only — a terminal with lived
outcomes ranks differently on purpose, and that is the privacy
boundary, not drift.
The bench wrote an outcome record for every task whether or not the
model ever produced anything. A mistyped adapter flag made all 11
tasks fail in ~10ms — no model was ever called — and the harness
emitted 11 rejections against worker:sonnet-4-5/code. Ingesting
those would have retired a worker on evidence it never had a chance
to earn, and the run still exited 0, so nothing would have noticed.
This is the front door's empty-stdout rule, which was already frozen,
arriving in the bench harness where it had never been applied: if the
verify command never ran, there is no evidence, only plumbing.
Attempts now carry blame; only blame=worker is scored and recorded,
harness failures are reported loudly, and a run that measured nothing
exits non-zero so CI cannot read it as a pass.
A runner is the user's own command line for a model, and the rules
for running one were learned from misattributed failures: the task
travels on stdin, the worker runs in a scratch directory that
inherits nothing, and empty stdout, a non-zero exit, a timeout or a
command that will not start are all the ENVIRONMENT's failure and
never the model's.
Those rules used to live as prose plus four near-copies of the same
code. That is how two identical bugs came to be fixed by hand in two
places while a third copy kept the bug. tools/owi_runner.py is now
the single implementation and returns a result whose blame is
explicit, so misattributing a plumbing failure takes a deliberate
misuse rather than a moment's inattention.
The last check is the one that keeps it true: no other tool may
spawn a worker itself.

failure_modes.name: a command that will not start

_why: The chat adapter turns a model's reply into a function body. It used
to drop everything through the first `def` line found at ANY
indentation, meaning to strip a restated signature. A body that opens
with a nested helper — `def _to_float_array(...)` inside the function
— lost that header and kept its indented block, so the spliced file
would not even import. Pytest said 'errors during collection', the
runner scored it as a failed implementation, and the ledger learned
that the model cannot code.
It was really measuring which models avoid nested helpers. That is a
style, not a capability. worker:opus-5/code scored 3/11 under the
broken rule, with 5 of its 8 failures being collection errors rather
than wrong answers; nothing from that run was recorded.
The rule now strips a restated signature only when it sits at column
zero AND names the function under test. Everything a body needs to
define for itself survives.
A second defect surfaced while freezing the first: extract_body called
reply.strip(), and leading whitespace on the first line IS the body's
indentation. Stripping it made the min-indent calculation see column
zero and shift every deeper line four spaces further in. Fenced replies
took an rstrip path and were unaffected, so the same answer normalised
differently depending on whether the model wrapped it in a code fence.

fixtures.name: a restated signature at column zero is stripped
a nested helper keeps its own def
a bare body at column zero is indented in
a different function keeps its header, indented in

_why: A bench outcome's id was a pure function of (corpus, worker, task).
That made a worker measurable on a corpus exactly ONCE: every later
run produced identical ids, the append-only ledger answered UNIQUE
constraint failed, and the outcomes were rejected one file at a time
while an ingest loop reported nothing at all.
It surfaced the day after the extraction bug was fixed. Re-benching
worker:haiku-4-5/code — retired from code on a 4/11 measured with the
broken harness — produced an honest 7/11 that the ledger silently
refused. Re-measurement is exactly what must work after a harness
fix, because every number taken before it is suspect.
The id now carries the run's own identity (its observed_at). The
ledger stays append-only: a new measurement is added ALONGSIDE the
old one, never over it, and the posterior moves because evidence
accumulated rather than because history was edited.
The roster shipped with assumed ability: every seeded evidence row
tagged vendor_reported, pointed at example.invalid, and discounted to
a tenth of its weight. The evidence importer is how measured numbers
replace them, and it mirrors the price importer because a claim about
ability deserves the same discipline as a claim about cost — the exact
bytes hashed before parsing, the models listed explicitly, provenance
on every record, and an append rather than an edit.
Two rules are pinned here because getting either wrong misstaffs work
rather than merely mislabelling a row.
Normalisation is explicit: a raw score is divided by a stated scale,
never guessed from its magnitude, and a score outside [0,1] after
scaling is skipped rather than clamped.
worker_id stays unset unless the source names a full configuration. A
leaderboard measures a model release; a worker is a release plus a
harness, skill pack, toolset and execution policy. Left unset the
score informs every worker on that release — which is why importing
battery-core results moved worker:openhands-sonnet-5/code, a worker
that has never been benchmarked, from 0.500 to 0.536.
